name: The Reckless Gambler
summary: High risk tolerance, no system, chases price, blows accounts and reloads.
common_mistakes: Revenge trading after losses
Doubling down on losing positions
Sizing up to chase a feeling
focus: Build a system before sizing up
Capital preservation comes before profit
Pre-defined position sizing rules

mmfx_path.cta_text: Start with the MM System eBook to learn the framework, then open a Team MM tier account with the broker to lock in accountability and structure.

keystone.label: Managing & Routine module
keystone.why: Build the risk rules first — fixed sizing and hard stops before anything else.

name: The Analysis Paralyser
summary: Over-thinks every setup, demands 100% confirmation, misses 80% of valid trades.
weaknesses: Chronic FOMO regret after missed moves
common_mistakes: Requiring more confirmation signals than the market ever gives
Waiting for the 'perfect' setup that never arrives
Talking themselves out of valid trades
focus: Probabilistic thinking — no setup is ever 100%
Defined entry criteria with a maximum count of conditions
Trade execution practice on demo, not endless backtesting

mmfx_path.cta_text: Read the Decision Tree eBook to externalise your entry criteria, then join MM Mentorship for accountability on actually executing those decisions live.

keystone.label: Backtest a strategy
keystone.why: Prove your rules work, so you stop demanding certainty that never comes.

name: The Signal Dependent
summary: Trades entirely off signals, no independent analysis skill.
weaknesses: Can't tell good signals from bad ones
common_mistakes: Taking signals without understanding why they were given
Following multiple signal providers with contradictory calls
Blaming the signal provider when trades lose
focus: Learning to validate signals against own analysis before executing
Building independent reasoning, not just execution
Understanding the structure behind each signal

mmfx_path.cta_text: Keep using the free signals, but pair them with the MM System eBook and Cheat Sheet so you can read the structure behind each call. Team MM is the structured path that turns signal-following into actual trading skill.

keystone.label: Start the MM System Course
keystone.why: Turn signal-following into a skill you actually own.

name: The Indicator Stacker
summary: Trades from a chart covered in 8+ indicators, mistakes complexity for edge, never sees clean price action.
weaknesses: Lagging indicators describe the past, they don't predict price
common_mistakes: Refusing to enter unless RSI, MACD, Stochastic and a moving average all agree
Adding more indicators when a system stops working
Mistaking indicator confluence for market confluence
focus: Reading raw market structure — highs, lows, order flow, liquidity
Deleting indicators that don't change your decision
Trusting price over derivatives of price

mmfx_path.cta_text: Read the MM System eBook — specifically the price-action and structure modules — and open a Team MM tier account to retrain on a clean-chart, SMC-based approach.

keystone.label: Reading Price module
keystone.why: Trade clean structure instead of a wall of contradicting indicators.

name: The Emotional Revenge Trader
summary: Wins lead to overconfidence, losses lead to tilt, account swings wildly between green and red.
strengths: Learns fast when not on tilt
Honest about own emotional pattern when calm
common_mistakes: Increasing position size after losses to 'win it back'
Trading immediately after a loss instead of stepping back
Treating one losing trade as a sign the whole system is broken
focus: Pre-defined daily loss limits with mandatory cool-down
Mandatory break after two consecutive losses
Journaling emotional state alongside trade outcomes

mmfx_path.cta_text: Read the If-Then eBook and Decision Tree, then join MM Mentorship for the accountability and psychology framework that turns rules into actual behaviour.

keystone.label: Read the If-Then eBook
keystone.why: Pre-commit your reactions so a loss cannot hijack you.

name: The News Trader
summary: Lives for NFP, FOMC, CPI — trades the volatility around scheduled events, sits on hands the rest of the time.
weaknesses: Gets caught by stop hunts in the first 30 seconds of a release
Treats every red headline as a tradable event
common_mistakes: Entering market orders into a news spike before liquidity returns
Filling at the worst possible price after a stop run
Holding through the second leg of a reversal because the news 'should have' moved it the other way
focus: Layering structure-based entries on top of news catalysts
Waiting for the post-news pullback rather than chasing the initial spike
Defining 'no-trade' windows around the release itself

mmfx_path.cta_text: Read the MM System eBook for structure entries and the Decision Tree for execution rules, then join MM Mentorship to combine macro and structure into one playbook.

keystone.label: Economic Calendar
keystone.why: Plan around the catalysts instead of chasing every headline.

name: The System Hopper
summary: Tries a new strategy every couple of weeks because nothing seems to work long enough to compound. Owns five courses, finished none.
weaknesses: Mistakes normal drawdown for 'the system doesn't work'
Never gives any approach the sample size it needs to prove itself
Lacks the patience to compound an edge
common_mistakes: Abandoning a strategy after 5–10 trades
Buying the next course before finishing the current one
Treating every losing streak as a signal to switch frameworks
focus: Pick one framework and trade it for 100+ trades minimum before judging
Journal every trade so you have real data, not feelings, to evaluate against
Stop buying the next thing until this one is finished

mmfx_path.cta_text: Commit to the MM System eBook and Cheat Sheet as your one framework. Join MM Mentorship for the accountability you'll need to actually stick with it.

keystone.label: Commit to one system
keystone.why: One framework, traded long enough to actually compound.

name: The Brand New Beginner
summary: No system, no losses yet, exploring trading for the first time.
common_mistakes: Starting real-money trading before understanding basic price action
Skipping the demo phase to 'feel the real pressure'
Following the loudest voice on social media
focus: Foundational education before any live trading
Demo account for 30+ days minimum
Learning to read structure before learning entries

mmfx_path.cta_text: Stay in the free tier. Read the four eBooks in order: MM System first for the framework, Cheat Sheet for quick reference, Decision Tree for entries, If-Then for psychology. Use the free signals to study real setups while you learn.

keystone.label: Start at Foundations
keystone.why: Build the base before you put any real money at risk.
